subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in configurable permission policy for agent-created user-facing files, and what write paths and default modes are in scope?
rationale: The request adds config surface and changes security-sensitive filesystem semantics across several tool write paths, so automation should not choose the permanent permission boundary.

options.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
options.body: Add an opt-in permission policy for user-facing outputs while explicitly excluding private OpenClaw state, config, credentials, auth, and session files.

options.title: Use fixed per-path defaults
options.body: Adjust only selected write paths such as managed media or sandbox-created files without adding a general config knob.

options.title: Document external permission management
options.body: Keep OpenClaw defaults unchanged and document OS/container ACL, user, group, or umask setup as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in permission policy for user-facing outputs while explicitly excluding private OpenClaw state, config, credentials, auth, and session files.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent filesystem guard and sandbox mutation history is the strongest match for deciding the safe permission boundary.
